questions.question_text: Rewrite $\cos 130^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.

options.why: Took the supplement but kept the positive sign; cosine is negative in Q2.
Changed cosine to sine when taking the supplement.
Subtracted $90^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting from $180^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$130^{\circ}$ is obtuse, so cosine is negative.
$\cos 130^{\circ}=-\cos(180^{\circ}-130^{\circ})$
$=-\cos 50^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: Rewrite $\sin 145^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.

options.why: Made sine negative, but sine is positive in the second quadrant.
Subtracted $90^{\circ}$ from $145^{\circ}$ to obtain $55^{\circ}$ instead of finding $180^{\circ}-145^{\circ}$.
Changed sine to cosine when taking the supplement.

questions.solution_text:
$145^{\circ}$ is obtuse, so sine is positive.
$\sin 145^{\circ}=\sin(180^{\circ}-145^{\circ})$
$=\sin 35^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: Rewrite $\tan 155^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.

options.why: Took the supplement but kept the positive sign; tangent is negative in Q2.
Subtracted $90^{\circ}$ from $155^{\circ}$ to obtain $65^{\circ}$ instead of finding $180^{\circ}-155^{\circ}$.
Attached the negative sign but did not take the supplement.

questions.solution_text:
$155^{\circ}$ is obtuse, so tangent is negative.
$\tan 155^{\circ}=-\tan(180^{\circ}-155^{\circ})$
$=-\tan 25^{\circ}$
